acceptedClaims.declaredStatement: For every input law on the governed half-skew BSSC product channel P^{otimes 2}, let c_in=P(X_1X_2=11)-Pr[X_1=1]Pr[X_2=1] and C_out=I(Y_1;Y_2)+I(Z_1;Z_2). A paired-receiver binary-table curvature argument proves the unconditional inequality C_out >= 31 c_in^2/(20 ln 2). Canonical transaction 9bb22afe5abd3e1d9f419c1717bd61bb33a958ff supplies the necessary inequality C_out < 7/160 for any finite two-letter Marton law whose unnormalized value exceeds twice the optimal one-letter randomized-time-division value. Consequently every such gain forces |c_in| < sqrt(7 ln 2/248) < 7/50. This is a necessary condition only; it does not construct a Marton gain, rule one out, tensorize Marton's functional, or give a capacity converse.
acceptedClaims.validitySummary: The paired binary-output-table argument establishes the unconditional bound C_out >= 31 c_in^2/(20 ln 2), including the boundary cases. The declared reference establishes that any finite two-letter Marton law exceeding twice the optimal one-letter randomized-time-division value has C_out < 7/160. Combining the bounds gives |c_in| < sqrt(7 ln 2/248) < 7/50. This remains only a necessary condition and does not construct or exclude a Marton gain, prove tensorization, or yield a capacity converse.
scopeQualifications: The conclusion applies to finite two-letter Marton laws whose unnormalized value exceeds twice the optimal one-letter randomized-time-division value.
The reference is required only for the Marton-gain implication C_out < 7/160; the curvature inequality is proved within the subject.
The result is solely a necessary covariance condition; it neither constructs nor rules out a gain, tensorizes Marton's functional, nor proves a capacity converse.
